"""Typed chapter content model of the offer workshop.

A chapter holds one of four content types. ``prose`` is the canonical block
tree, ``table`` a plain grid, ``stories`` only settings (the text is resolved
from the story map when rendering) and ``calc`` bound commercial values.
Anything outside this model is rejected with a German message.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import (
    AfterValidator,
    BaseModel,
    Field,
    TypeAdapter,
    ValidationError,
    ValidationInfo,
    field_validator,
)
from pydantic_core import ErrorDetails

BOUND_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
    "offer.person_days": "Personentage",
    "offer.risk_buffer_days": "Risikopuffer (Personentage)",
    "offer.production_cost": "Herstellkosten",
    "offer.recommended_price": "Empfohlener Preis",
    "workspace.currency": "Währung",
    "workspace.validity_date": "Bindefrist",
}


class ContentValidationError(ValueError):
    """Chapter content violates the content model; messages are German."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__("; ".join(messages))
        self.messages = messages


def _new_block_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]


class Run(BaseModel):
    text: str
    bold: bool = False
    italic: bool = False


Inline = list[Run]


class _Block(BaseModel):
    block_id: str = Field(default_factory=_new_block_id)


class Paragraph(_Block):
    type: Literal["paragraph"] = "paragraph"
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class Heading(_Block):
    type: Literal["heading"] = "heading"
    level: Literal[3, 4] = 3
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class BulletList(_Block):
    type: Literal["bullet_list"] = "bullet_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class OrderedList(_Block):
    type: Literal["ordered_list"] = "ordered_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableBlock(_Block):
    type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    header: list[Inline] = Field(min_length=1)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_header(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: ValidationInfo
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        _check_row_width(rows, len(info.data.get("header", [])), "die Kopfzeile")
        return rows


def _check_bound_field(value: str) -> str:
    if value not in BOUND_FIELDS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Kalkulationswert: {value}")
    return value


BoundFieldName = Annotated[str, AfterValidator(_check_bound_field)]


def _check_row_width(rows: list[list[Inline]], width: int, what: str) -> None:
    if any(len(row) != width for row in rows):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Jede Tabellenzeile braucht genau so viele Zellen wie {what}."
        )


class BoundValue(_Block):
    type: Literal["bound_value"] = "bound_value"
    field: BoundFieldName


ProseBlock = Annotated[
    Paragraph | Heading | BulletList | OrderedList | TableBlock | BoundValue,
    Field(discriminator="type"),
]


class ProseContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["prose"] = "prose"
    blocks: list[ProseBlock] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_columns(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: ValidationInfo
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        _check_row_width(rows, len(info.data.get("columns", [])), "Spalten")
        return rows


class StoriesContent(BaseModel):
    """Settings only; all live stories of the map revision, resolved at render time.

    Stored content from before may still carry ``scopes``; it is ignored.
    """

    chapter_type: Literal["stories"] = "stories"
    group_by: Literal["activity", "slice"] = "activity"


class CalcRow(BaseModel):
    label: str
    field: BoundFieldName


class CalcContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["calc"] = "calc"
    intro: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)
    rows: list[CalcRow] = Field(default_factory=list)


ChapterContent = Annotated[
    ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent,
    Field(discriminator="chapter_type"),
]

_CONTENT_ADAPTER: TypeAdapter[
    ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent
] = TypeAdapter(ChapterContent)


def plain_text(runs: Inline) -> str:
    return "".join(run.text for run in runs)


def parse_content(
    data: dict,
) -> ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent:
    """Validate raw JSON content; raise ``ContentValidationError`` in German."""
    try:
        return _CONTENT_ADAPTER.validate_python(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise ContentValidationError([_german(err) for err in exc.errors()]) from exc


def _german(error: ErrorDetails) -> str:
    message = str(error.get("msg", ""))
    if message.startswith("Value error, "):
        return message.removeprefix("Value error, ")
    location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
    if error.get("type") == "union_tag_invalid":
        if error.get("loc") == ():
            return "Unbekannter Kapiteltyp."
        return f"Nicht unterstützter Inhaltsbaustein ({location})."
    return f"Ungültiger Inhalt ({location})."

async def mark_chapters_review(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, keys: list[str], reason: str
) -> None:
    """Flag the chapters with ``keys`` for a new look."""
    if not keys:
        return
    await session.execute(
        update(ChapterEntity)
        .where(
            ChapterEntity.offer_id == offer_id,
            ChapterEntity.chapter_key.in_(keys),
        )
        .values(needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)
    )


async def mark_dependent_review(
    session: AsyncSession, workspace: WorkspaceEntity, reason: str = REVIEW_AFTER_MAP
) -> None:
    """Flag written prose chapters after a map change (A09, A27).

    Chapters that still hold the template text have nothing to review, and
    projections (stories, calc) follow the map by themselves.
    """
    prose = [c.key for c in _template(workspace).chapters if c.chapter_type == "prose"]
    await session.execute(
        update(ChapterEntity)
        .where(
            ChapterEntity.offer_id == workspace.offer_id,
            ChapterEntity.chapter_key.in_(prose),
            ChapterEntity.revision > 1,
        )
        .values(needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)
    )


async def find_chapter(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, key: str, *, lock: bool = False
) -> ChapterEntity:
    query = select(ChapterEntity).where(
        ChapterEntity.offer_id == offer_id, ChapterEntity.chapter_key == key
    )
    chapter = await session.scalar(query.with_for_update() if lock else query)
    if chapter is None:
        raise ChapterError(NOT_FOUND)
    return chapter

    session: AsyncSession, chapter: ChapterEntity, number: int | None = None
) -> ChapterRevisionEntity:
    revision = await session.scalar(
        select(ChapterRevisionEntity).where(
            ChapterRevisionEntity.chapter_id == chapter.id,
            ChapterRevisionEntity.number == (number or chapter.revision),
        )
    )
    if revision is None:
        raise ChapterError(NO_REVISION)
    return revision

"""Chapters of an offer: revisions, conflicts and AI proposals (spec 5.5, 10.2-10.4).

A chapter's text lives in immutable revisions. A save names the revision the person
saw; if somebody saved in between, nothing is overwritten (A08). AI texts only ever
arrive as proposals that a person accepts.
"""

import logging
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select, tuple_, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.content.schema import ProseContent, parse_content
from alloq_offer.workshop.content.text import Content, diff_lines, stored_lines
from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    ChapterEntity,

    ChapterRevisionEntity,
    FindingDecision,
    FindingEntity,
    ProposalEntity,
    ProposalStatus,
    WorkspaceEntity,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import (
    ChapterDef,
    TemplatePackage,
    load_template,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import workspace_repo

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

CONFLICT = (
    "Das Kapitel wurde inzwischen geändert. Die aktuelle Fassung wurde geladen, "
    "bitte wiederholen Sie die Änderung."
)
NOT_FOUND = "Das Kapitel gibt es nicht."
PROTECTED = "Das Kapitel ist geschützt. Heben Sie den Schutz auf, um es zu ändern."
WRONG_TYPE = "Dieser Inhalt passt nicht zum Typ des Kapitels."
NO_PROPOSAL = "Der Vorschlag gibt es nicht mehr."
STALE_PROPOSAL = (
    "Der Vorschlag ist veraltet, weil das Kapitel inzwischen geändert wurde."
)
REVIEW_AFTER_MAP = "Die Story Map hat sich seit dem Verfassen geändert."
NO_REVISION = "Diese Fassung gibt es nicht."


class ChapterConflictError(RuntimeError):
    """Somebody saved the chapter since this editor loaded it (A08)."""


class ChapterError(ValueError):
    """The change is not allowed; the message is German and shown to users."""


def default_content(definition: ChapterDef) -> Content:
    """The empty content a chapter starts with, from the template defaults."""
    return parse_content(
        {"chapter_type": definition.chapter_type, **definition.defaults}
    )


def _template(workspace: WorkspaceEntity) -> TemplatePackage:
    return load_template(workspace.template_key)


async def mark_chapters_review(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, keys: list[str], reason: str
) -> None:
    """Flag the chapters with ``keys`` for a new look."""
    if not keys:
        return
    await session.execute(
        update(ChapterEntity)
        .where(
            ChapterEntity.offer_id == offer_id,
            ChapterEntity.chapter_key.in_(keys),
        )
        .values(needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)
    )


async def mark_dependent_review(
    session: AsyncSession, workspace: WorkspaceEntity, reason: str = REVIEW_AFTER_MAP
) -> None:
    """Flag written prose chapters after a map change (A09, A27).

    Chapters that still hold the template text have nothing to review, and
    projections (stories, calc) follow the map by themselves.
    """
    prose = [c.key for c in _template(workspace).chapters if c.chapter_type == "prose"]
    await session.execute(
        update(ChapterEntity)
        .where(
            ChapterEntity.offer_id == workspace.offer_id,
            ChapterEntity.chapter_key.in_(prose),
            ChapterEntity.revision > 1,
        )
        .values(needs_review=True, review_reason=reason)
    )


async def find_chapter(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, key: str, *, lock: bool = False
) -> ChapterEntity:
    query = select(ChapterEntity).where(
        ChapterEntity.offer_id == offer_id, ChapterEntity.chapter_key == key
    )
    chapter = await session.scalar(query.with_for_update() if lock else query)
    if chapter is None:
        raise ChapterError(NOT_FOUND)
    return chapter


async def revision_of(
    session: AsyncSession, chapter: ChapterEntity, number: int | None = None
) -> ChapterRevisionEntity:
    revision = await session.scalar(
        select(ChapterRevisionEntity).where(
            ChapterRevisionEntity.chapter_id == chapter.id,
            ChapterRevisionEntity.number == (number or chapter.revision),
        )
    )
    if revision is None:
        raise ChapterError(NO_REVISION)
    return revision


def _without_block_ids(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _without_block_ids(v) for k, v in value.items() if k != "block_id"}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_without_block_ids(v) for v in value]
    return value

"""Template package: chapter catalogue, rules and Word layout of one template."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
from functools import cache, cached_property
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

import yaml
from docx import Document
from docx.document import Document as DocxDocument
from docx.text.paragraph import Paragraph as DocxParagraph
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

TEMPLATES_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "templates"
DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY = "quo_v1"
CHAPTER_ANCHOR = "[[KAPITEL]]"


class TemplateError(ValueError):
    """The template package is inconsistent."""


class ChapterDef(BaseModel):
    key: str
    title: str
    level: Literal[1, 2] = 1
    required: bool = False
    chapter_type: Literal["prose", "table", "stories", "calc"]
    defaults: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    guiding_question: str = ""
    content_rules: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TemplatePackage(BaseModel):
    key: str
    version: str
    chapters: list[ChapterDef]
    static_chapters: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    rules: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    layout_path: Path

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _unique_keys(self) -> TemplatePackage:
        keys = [chapter.key for chapter in self.chapters]
        if len(keys) != len(set(keys)):
            raise TemplateError("Kapitelschlüssel müssen eindeutig sein.")
        return self

    def chapter(self, key: str) -> ChapterDef:
        for chapter in self.chapters:
            if chapter.key == key:
                return chapter
        raise KeyError(key)

    @cached_property
    def layout_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return self.layout_path.read_bytes()

    def check_layout(self) -> None:
        """Fail unless the layout holds the chapter anchor exactly once."""
        document = Document(io.BytesIO(self.layout_bytes))
        anchors = [p for p in document.paragraphs if p.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR]
        if len(anchors) != 1:
            raise TemplateError(
                f"Die Vorlage braucht genau einen Anker {CHAPTER_ANCHOR}."
            )


def find_anchor(document: DocxDocument) -> DocxParagraph:
    for paragraph in document.paragraphs:
        if paragraph.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR:
            return paragraph
    raise TemplateError(f"Die Vorlage braucht genau einen Anker {CHAPTER_ANCHOR}.")


@cache
def load_template(
    key: str = DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY, root: Path = TEMPLATES_ROOT
) -> TemplatePackage:
    base = root / key
    chapters_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "chapters.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rules_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "rules.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    package = TemplatePackage(
        key=key,
        version=chapters_doc["version"],
        chapters=[ChapterDef(**item) for item in chapters_doc["chapters"]],
        static_chapters=chapters_doc.get("static_chapters", []),
        rules=rules_doc.get("chapters", {}),
        layout_path=base / "layout.docx",
    )
    package.check_layout()
    return package

                return chapter
        raise KeyError(key)

    def layout_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return self.layout_path.read_bytes()

    def check_layout(self) -> None:
        """Fail unless the layout holds the chapter anchor exactly once."""
        document = Document(io.BytesIO(self.layout_bytes))
        anchors = [p for p in document.paragraphs if p.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR]
        if len(anchors) != 1:
            raise TemplateError(
                f"Die Vorlage braucht genau einen Anker {CHAPTER_ANCHOR}."
            )


def find_anchor(document: DocxDocument) -> DocxParagraph:
    for paragraph in document.paragraphs:
        if paragraph.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR:
            return paragraph
    raise TemplateError(f"Die Vorlage braucht genau einen Anker {CHAPTER_ANCHOR}.")

def load_template(
    key: str = DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY, root: Path = TEMPLATES_ROOT
) -> TemplatePackage:
    base = root / key
    chapters_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "chapters.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rules_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "rules.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    package = TemplatePackage(
        key=key,
        version=chapters_doc["version"],
        chapters=[ChapterDef(**item) for item in chapters_doc["chapters"]],
        static_chapters=chapters_doc.get("static_chapters", []),
        rules=rules_doc.get("chapters", {}),
        layout_path=base / "layout.docx",
    )
    package.check_layout()
    return package

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons import theme
from alloq_commons.components.shell import app_page
from alloq_commons.components.toolbar import window_toolbar
from alloq_offer.components.industry import industries_table, industries_toolbar
from alloq_offer.states.industry_state import IndustryState

import appkit_mantine as mn
from appkit_user.authentication.components.components import requires_admin


def create_industries_page(
    sidebar: rx.Component,
    route: str = "/admin/industries",
    title: str = "Branchen",
) -> rx.Component:
    """Page factory for the industries offers can use."""

    @app_page(
        route=route,
        title=title,
        sidebar=sidebar,
        toolbar=window_toolbar(
            "Branchen",
            "Administration · Branchen für Angebote pflegen",
            actions=industries_toolbar(),
        ),
        admin_only=True,
        on_load=[IndustryState.load_industries],
    )
    def _industries_page() -> rx.Component:
        return requires_admin(
            mn.box(
                industries_table(),
                style=theme.CARD,
                p="xs",
                w="100%",
                max_width="1200px",
            ),
        )

    return _industries_page

52:Eine webbasierte Angebotswerkstatt führt E-Mails, Gesprächsmitschnitte, Konzepte und Präsentationen in einem gemeinsamen Angebotsarbeitsraum zusammen. Ihr fachlicher Mittelpunkt sind die **Kundenprozesse, die durch das Projekt umgesetzt oder verändert werden sollen**. Die Anwendung erkennt Rollen, Ziele, Aktivitäten und Aufgaben, erstellt daraus eine User Story Map mit einfachen User Stories und leitet daraus einen kapitelweisen Angebotsentwurf ab. Nutzer überarbeiten Map, Stories und Kapitel im Browser. Anschließend entsteht ein editierbares Word-Dokument auf Grundlage der vorhandenen Vorlage.
54:Empfohlen wird ein **iterativer fachlicher Entwurfsprozess mit klaren technischen Zuständigkeiten und menschlicher Entscheidungshoheit**. Die Anwendung steuert Speicherung, Versionen, Berechtigungen und Export verlässlich. Sprachmodelle helfen beim Verstehen unvollständiger Eingaben, beim Rekonstruieren und Entwerfen von Prozessen, beim Formulieren von Stories und beim Erarbeiten einer passenden Lösung. Die fachliche Arbeit darf zwischen Quellen, Map, Stories und Kapiteltext zurückspringen.
58:> Die User Story Map mit ihren einfachen Stories ist das erste fachliche Startartefakt und die gemeinsame Grundlage für Leistungsumfang, Lösung und Angebotskapitel. Kundenmaterial, neue Nutzerentscheidungen und fachliche Entwurfsarbeit treiben den Inhalt. Unternehmenswissen ergänzt bei Bedarf. Die Anwendung verwaltet den verbindlichen Bearbeitungsstand und überführt ihn in die vorhandene Word-Vorlage.
73:- Kapitel werden auf einer Webseite angezeigt und können dort bearbeitet werden.
83:- Ein verantwortlicher Bearbeiter je Kapitel zur selben Zeit; gleichzeitige Live-Zusammenarbeit ist zunächst nicht erforderlich.
84:- Deutsch als erste Ausgabesprache. Sprache und Stil werden später über das Vorlagenpaket erweitert.
85:- Zunächst eine konkrete Word-Vorlage produktiv anbinden. Weitere Vorlagen verwenden dasselbe Vertrags- und Prüfmodell.
90:Die tatsächliche Word-Datei wurde für dieses Konzept noch nicht untersucht. Deshalb sind konkrete Kapitel, Formatierungsregeln und technische Einschränkungen der Vorlage vor der Umsetzung zu prüfen. Die Beispielgliederung in Abschnitt 6 ersetzt diese Prüfung nicht.
100:| WW-KonzAI | Strukturierte Matrix mit Quellen und Hinweisen | Versionierte Story Map als Verbindung zwischen Quellen, Stories, Leistungsumfang und Kapiteln |
101:| WW-KonzAI | Dokumentaufbau durch Anwendungscode | Word-Export aus einem festen Bearbeitungsstand mit versionierter Vorlage |
103:Die wichtigste fachliche Abweichung ist der Ausgangspunkt: Das Kundenprojekt wird aus seinen Anforderungen und Prozessen entworfen. Bereits vorhandene Unternehmensleistungen oder Angebotstexte bestimmen diesen Entwurf nicht. Hinzu kommen ein Map- und Story-Editor, ein Kapitel-Editor, der Schutz manueller Änderungen, die Übernahme der Word-Vorlage und ein belastbarer Umgang mit kommerziellen Aussagen.
129:    F --> G[Kapitel im Browser bearbeiten]
130:    G --> H[Gesamtstand aus Map, Stories und Kapiteln prüfen]
139:Nutzer vergeben einen Namen und ordnen den Kunden zu. Das vorhandene Vorlagenpaket ist voreingestellt oder auswählbar. Die leere Story-Map-Ansicht bildet den Einstieg. Optionale Felder sind Ansprechpartner, Angebotsart, Termin, Sprache und Vertriebsreferenz. Fehlende Angaben verhindern das Anlegen nicht; sie werden nicht durch erfundene Prozessinhalte ersetzt.
157:### 5.5 Kapitel erstellen und bearbeiten
159:Erst auf Basis einer versionierten Map werden die Kapitel der Vorlage entworfen. Nutzer können Texte und Tabellen bearbeiten, Abschnitte ergänzen und gezielt KI-Vorschläge anfordern. Die zugehörigen Stories bleiben erreichbar. Map und Story-Katalog sind gespeicherte Fachobjekte; ihre Darstellung im Kapiteltext ist eine Projektion desselben Stands.
161:Neue Vorschläge erscheinen als Vergleich zum aktuellen Stand. Erst die Übernahme ändert den verbindlichen Inhalt. Ein leeres Unternehmenswissensarchiv verhindert weder Map noch Stories oder Kapitelentwurf.
165:Vor dem Export werden alle Änderungen gespeichert und ein fester Dokumentstand gebildet. Der Nutzer sieht die Ausgabeart und vorhandene Blocker. Der Export verwendet diesen Stand sowie die zugeordnete Version der Word-Vorlage. Spätere Bearbeitungen verändern eine bereits erzeugte Datei nicht.
167:## 6. Vorlagenmodell: vorhandenes Word und bearbeitbare Kapitel
169:### 6.1 Ein versioniertes Vorlagenpaket
171:Ein Vorlagenpaket besteht aus drei zusammengehörigen Teilen:
175:| Kapiteldefinition | Stabile Kapitel-IDs, Pflichtstatus und Inhaltsregeln; die User Story Map beginnt den fachlichen Inhalt, gefolgt von verknüpften Stories und Angebotskapiteln |
176:| Word-Layoutdatei | Bestehende Corporate-Vorlage mit Formatvorlagen, Kopf- und Fußzeilen, Platzhaltern und wiederholbaren Bereichen |
179:Alle Teile werden gemeinsam versioniert und auf Kompatibilität geprüft. Ein Angebot bindet eine konkrete Paketversion. Ein Vorlagenwechsel ist eine ausdrückliche Migration mit Vorschau; er verändert vorhandene Angebote nicht automatisch.
181:### 6.2 Übernahme der bestehenden Word-Vorlage
183:1. **Inventarisieren:** Kapitel, Formatvorlagen, Tabellen, Nummerierung, Inhaltsverzeichnis, Abschnitte, Bilder, Pflichtformulierungen und Formularfelder erfassen. Die User Story Map mit verknüpftem Story-Katalog am Beginn des fachlichen Inhalts verankern; fehlt dieser Bereich, wird die Vorlage gezielt ergänzt.
185:3. **Technisch vorbereiten:** Geeignete Platzhalter und Wiederholungsbereiche in einer Kopie der Vorlage ergänzen. Generierter Inhalt darf keine neue Vorlagenlogik ausführen.
186:4. **Fähigkeiten testen:** Eine Referenzdatei mit kurzen und langen Kapiteln, Tabellen, Listen und Sonderzeichen erzeugen. Mit der Ausgangsvorlage in Word vergleichen.
187:5. **Paket freigeben:** Nur geprüfte Kombinationen aus Layout, Kapiteldefinition und Exporter werden angeboten.
189:Ein automatischer Erstvorschlag für die Kapitelzuordnung ist möglich. Die beliebige, verlustfreie Umwandlung jeder Word-Datei in einen Webeditor wird nicht vorausgesetzt. Komplexe Textfelder, verschachtelte Tabellen, spezielle Nummerierung und eingebettete Objekte können eine Anpassung der Vorlage erfordern.
193:Die vorhandene Vorlage bleibt die Layoutgrundlage. Die Vorgabe, fachlich mit einer Story Map zu beginnen, wird bei ihrer Übernahme ausdrücklich umgesetzt. Folgende Inhalte dienen als Zuordnungshilfe:
208:Wiederverwendbarkeit entsteht durch Vorlagen und fachliche Inhaltsprofile. AI-, Agenten- oder Data-Science-Angebote können zusätzliche Leitfragen erhalten, ohne die gesamte Verarbeitungskette auszutauschen.
248:Zwischen Kundeneingaben und Angebotskapiteln liegt ein leichtgewichtiges fachliches Modell. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Kundenprozesse und die daraus abgeleiteten einfachen User Stories. Die Map wird vor den Kapiteln angelegt und über den gesamten Entwurfsprozess gepflegt.
315:`Kundenbedarf / Prozessquelle → Aktivität → Aufgabe → einfache User Story → angebotener Umfang → Kapitel`
327:| Angebot | Kunde, Eigentümer, Berechtigungen, Sprache, Vorlagenpaket, Map-Revision und aktueller Dokumentstand |
337:| Kapitelrevision | Stabile Kapitel-ID, strukturierter Inhalt, Bearbeiter und Ausgangsrevision |
338:| Generierungslauf | Quellen-, Prozess-, Map- und Kapitelstände, Modell-/Promptversion, optionaler Wissenskontext, Status und Vorschläge |
340:| Export | Feste Dokumentrevision, Vorlagenversion, Exporterversion und erzeugte Datei |
346:Bestätigte Preise, Termine und andere wiederholte Stammdaten werden über gebundene Werte im Kapitelbaum dargestellt. Sie referenzieren ein Feld des Angebotsmodells und werden im Browser sowie in Word aus derselben Revision aufgelöst. Änderungen an diesen Werten erfolgen im zugehörigen Fachformular; eine erneute KI-Formulierung darf sie nicht ersetzen.
348:Map und Stories werden im Map-/Story-Editor bearbeitet und haben jeweils einen verbindlichen Revisionsstand. Ihre Darstellungen in Kapiteln und Word werden daraus abgeleitet; es gibt keinen zweiten unabhängig gepflegten Story-Katalog im Fließtext. Das Ändern einer Story löscht keine manuelle Kapitelüberarbeitung, sondern markiert betroffene Kapitel und Scope-Angaben zur erneuten Prüfung.

159:Erst auf Basis einer versionierten Map werden die Kapitel der Vorlage entworfen. Nutzer können Texte und Tabellen bearbeiten, Abschnitte ergänzen und gezielt KI-Vorschläge anfordern. Die zugehörigen Stories bleiben erreichbar. Map und Story-Katalog sind gespeicherte Fachobjekte; ihre Darstellung im Kapiteltext ist eine Projektion desselben Stands.
161:Neue Vorschläge erscheinen als Vergleich zum aktuellen Stand. Erst die Übernahme ändert den verbindlichen Inhalt. Ein leeres Unternehmenswissensarchiv verhindert weder Map noch Stories oder Kapitelentwurf.
165:Vor dem Export werden alle Änderungen gespeichert und ein fester Dokumentstand gebildet. Der Nutzer sieht die Ausgabeart und vorhandene Blocker. Der Export verwendet diesen Stand sowie die zugeordnete Version der Word-Vorlage. Spätere Bearbeitungen verändern eine bereits erzeugte Datei nicht.
167:## 6. Vorlagenmodell: vorhandenes Word und bearbeitbare Kapitel
169:### 6.1 Ein versioniertes Vorlagenpaket
171:Ein Vorlagenpaket besteht aus drei zusammengehörigen Teilen:
175:| Kapiteldefinition | Stabile Kapitel-IDs, Pflichtstatus und Inhaltsregeln; die User Story Map beginnt den fachlichen Inhalt, gefolgt von verknüpften Stories und Angebotskapiteln |
176:| Word-Layoutdatei | Bestehende Corporate-Vorlage mit Formatvorlagen, Kopf- und Fußzeilen, Platzhaltern und wiederholbaren Bereichen |
179:Alle Teile werden gemeinsam versioniert und auf Kompatibilität geprüft. Ein Angebot bindet eine konkrete Paketversion. Ein Vorlagenwechsel ist eine ausdrückliche Migration mit Vorschau; er verändert vorhandene Angebote nicht automatisch.
181:### 6.2 Übernahme der bestehenden Word-Vorlage
183:1. **Inventarisieren:** Kapitel, Formatvorlagen, Tabellen, Nummerierung, Inhaltsverzeichnis, Abschnitte, Bilder, Pflichtformulierungen und Formularfelder erfassen. Die User Story Map mit verknüpftem Story-Katalog am Beginn des fachlichen Inhalts verankern; fehlt dieser Bereich, wird die Vorlage gezielt ergänzt.
185:3. **Technisch vorbereiten:** Geeignete Platzhalter und Wiederholungsbereiche in einer Kopie der Vorlage ergänzen. Generierter Inhalt darf keine neue Vorlagenlogik ausführen.
186:4. **Fähigkeiten testen:** Eine Referenzdatei mit kurzen und langen Kapiteln, Tabellen, Listen und Sonderzeichen erzeugen. Mit der Ausgangsvorlage in Word vergleichen.
187:5. **Paket freigeben:** Nur geprüfte Kombinationen aus Layout, Kapiteldefinition und Exporter werden angeboten.
189:Ein automatischer Erstvorschlag für die Kapitelzuordnung ist möglich. Die beliebige, verlustfreie Umwandlung jeder Word-Datei in einen Webeditor wird nicht vorausgesetzt. Komplexe Textfelder, verschachtelte Tabellen, spezielle Nummerierung und eingebettete Objekte können eine Anpassung der Vorlage erfordern.
193:Die vorhandene Vorlage bleibt die Layoutgrundlage. Die Vorgabe, fachlich mit einer Story Map zu beginnen, wird bei ihrer Übernahme ausdrücklich umgesetzt. Folgende Inhalte dienen als Zuordnungshilfe:
208:Wiederverwendbarkeit entsteht durch Vorlagen und fachliche Inhaltsprofile. AI-, Agenten- oder Data-Science-Angebote können zusätzliche Leitfragen erhalten, ohne die gesamte Verarbeitungskette auszutauschen.
248:Zwischen Kundeneingaben und Angebotskapiteln liegt ein leichtgewichtiges fachliches Modell. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Kundenprozesse und die daraus abgeleiteten einfachen User Stories. Die Map wird vor den Kapiteln angelegt und über den gesamten Entwurfsprozess gepflegt.
315:`Kundenbedarf / Prozessquelle → Aktivität → Aufgabe → einfache User Story → angebotener Umfang → Kapitel`
327:| Angebot | Kunde, Eigentümer, Berechtigungen, Sprache, Vorlagenpaket, Map-Revision und aktueller Dokumentstand |
337:| Kapitelrevision | Stabile Kapitel-ID, strukturierter Inhalt, Bearbeiter und Ausgangsrevision |
338:| Generierungslauf | Quellen-, Prozess-, Map- und Kapitelstände, Modell-/Promptversion, optionaler Wissenskontext, Status und Vorschläge |
340:| Export | Feste Dokumentrevision, Vorlagenversion, Exporterversion und erzeugte Datei |
346:Bestätigte Preise, Termine und andere wiederholte Stammdaten werden über gebundene Werte im Kapitelbaum dargestellt. Sie referenzieren ein Feld des Angebotsmodells und werden im Browser sowie in Word aus derselben Revision aufgelöst. Änderungen an diesen Werten erfolgen im zugehörigen Fachformular; eine erneute KI-Formulierung darf sie nicht ersetzen.
348:Map und Stories werden im Map-/Story-Editor bearbeitet und haben jeweils einen verbindlichen Revisionsstand. Ihre Darstellungen in Kapiteln und Word werden daraus abgeleitet; es gibt keinen zweiten unabhängig gepflegten Story-Katalog im Fließtext. Das Ändern einer Story löscht keine manuelle Kapitelüberarbeitung, sondern markiert betroffene Kapitel und Scope-Angaben zur erneuten Prüfung.

options.label: Blank only

The "Kapitel" tab of the offer workshop is a three-column list/editor/inspector today. Each
chapter is edited on its own, the outline is fixed by `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, and
chapter prompts are hard-wired. The prototype (screenshot "KI-gestützte Bearbeitung von
Kundenanfragen") shows the target: one continuous document that feels like a word processor,
an outline that the team can extend and reorder, and a context panel per chapter type.
Admins must be able to build templates from reusable chapter blocks and maintain the AI
prompts without a code change.

The work is large. Implement it in the phases below, one phase per commit, each phase green
on `task lint`, `task typecheck` and `task test` before the next starts.

---

## Task
1. Rebuild the Kapitel tab as a document view like the prototype: outline left, all
   chapters as stacked blocks in the middle, a chapter panel right. Only the selected
   chapter is editable and shows its own toolbar.
2. Let users add chapters (from the library or blank), remove optional ones, and reorder
   them by drag and drop. Required chapters cannot be removed. The fixed legal frame of the
   Word layout stays pinned at start and end.
3. Move templates, reusable chapter blocks, rule checks, the Word layout and all AI prompts
   from code files into the database, edited in one new admin menu "Angebote".

## Load first
`alloq-implementation` (mandatory), then `reflex-state-and-architecture`,
`appkit-mantine-reference`, `appkit-commons`, `reflex-testing-state`, `german-ui-copy`.

## Existing code to build on (all under `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/`)
| Area | Files | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Template loader | `export/template_package.py` | `load_template(key)` (cached) builds `TemplatePackage` from YAML + `layout.docx`; `ChapterDef`, `CHAPTER_ANCHOR`, `check_layout()` |
| Template call sites | `services/chapters.py`, `services/findings.py`, `services/workspace.py`, `services/export_snapshot.py`, `jobs/draft_chapters.py`, `jobs/export_docx.py` | All call `load_template(workspace.template_key)` |
| Template data | `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, `rules.yaml`, `layout.docx` | Layout holds the legal frame (Rechtlicher Hinweis, Inhaltsverzeichnis before `[[KAPITEL]]`; Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist, Sonstiges, Anlagen, Unterschriften after) |
| Content model | `content/schema.py`, `content/editor_io.py`, `content/text.py` | Types `prose`, `table`, `stories`, `calc`; HTML ⇄ block tree |
| Chapters service | `services/chapters.py` | Revisions, conflict check (A08), proposals, protection, `default_content()`, `mark_dependent_review()` |
| Chapter state / UI | `states/chapter_state.py`, `components/chapters_tab.py`, `components/review_panel.py` | Autosave with debounce, AI help, history, findings |
| Entities | `entities.py` | `WorkspaceEntity.template_key/template_version`, `ChapterEntity` (unique `offer_id, chapter_key`), `ChapterRevisionEntity`, `ProposalEntity`, `FindingEntity`, `SnapshotEntity`, `BlobEntity` |
| Blob storage | `storage.py`, `BlobEntity` | Reuse for uploaded layout files |
| Prompts | `ai/agents.py` (`load_prompt`, `*_PROMPT` names, `*_prompt_version` attrs), `ai/prompts/*.md`, `ai/render.py`, `ai/port.py`, `ai/demo.py` | `GenerationRunEntity` records the prompt version |
| Export | `export/docx_renderer.py`, `export/chapter_renderers.py` | Uses `chapter.title/level` from the snapshot |
| Admin pages | `app/pages/industries.py` (pattern: `app_page(..., admin_only=True)`, `window_toolbar`, `requires_admin`), `app/components/sidebar.py` (`ADMIN` nav list) | |
| Editor | `mn.rich_text_editor` (`appkit_mantine/tiptap.py`) has `show_toolbar`, `sticky`, `sticky_offset`, `editable`, `control_groups` | |
| Theme/CSS | `alloq_commons/theme.py`, `assets/css/aq-workshop.css` | |

Repo rules that apply (from memory and CLAUDE.md):
- Offers are edited by `offer_editor` only (`requires_offer_editor`), admins do not edit offers.
  The admin menu needs the admin switch (`requires_admin` on the page and on every handler).
- Big state logic goes into mixins, not substates. Keep DB handlers in the module tests patch.
- Static layout CSS goes in `assets/css/aq-*.css`. Page popovers use `theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX`.
- Hand-written Alembic revisions in `alembic/versions/` (date-prefixed names). Never run
  `alembic upgrade`; hand the command to the user. Run the `migration-reviewer` agent.
- Sort German names in Python, not in SQL. Files ≤ 1000 lines. No f-strings in logger calls.
- German UI text, Sie-form, as in the existing tab.

---

## Decisions (agreed with the user)
- **Frame:** the legal blocks from the Word layout stay pinned at start and end and cannot
  be moved or removed. Required content chapters can be moved but not removed. Optional and
  added chapters can be moved and removed.
- **"+ Kapitel"** offers library blocks (with default content, rules and prompt) and a blank
  chapter of a chosen type (Text, Tabelle, User Stories, Werte).
- **Prompts:** global system prompts (chapter, map, map additions, briefing, review) are
  editable and versioned in admin. Each library block adds its own instructions on top
  (Leitfrage, Regeln, extra prompt text).
- **Admin scope now:** templates, chapter blocks, prompts, Word layout upload, rule checks.
  Branchen stays on its own page.
- **Template changes never alter existing offers** (spec 6.1). A template is edited as a
  draft and published as an immutable version. A workspace binds `template_key` +
  `template_version`. On creation the offer copies the outline and chapter settings into its
  own chapters.

---

## Phase 1: Data model and migration
New entities in a new module `workshop/template_entities.py` (keeps `entities.py` under the
line limit):
- `ChapterBlockEntity` (`offer_chapter_blocks`): `key` (unique slug), `title`,
  `chapter_type`, `level` (1 or 2), `default_content` (JSON, validated by `parse_content`),
  `guiding_question`, `content_rules` (JSON list), `prompt_text`, `required_info` (JSON list),
  `checks` (JSON list, values limited to the check names known in `services/checks.py`),
  `active`.
- `OfferTemplateEntity` (`offer_templates`): `key` (unique), `name`, `description`, `active`,
  `draft_layout_blob_id`, `frame_before` / `frame_after` (JSON lists of headings).
- `OfferTemplateChapterEntity` (`offer_template_chapters`): `template_id`, `block_id`,
  `position`, `required`, optional `title` and `level` overrides. Draft outline only.
- `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` (`offer_template_versions`): `template_id`, `number`,
  `payload` (JSON: full outline with resolved block settings, frame lists), `layout_blob_id`,
  `published_by`, `created`. Immutable.
- `PromptEntity` (`offer_prompts`): `name` (chapter, map, map_additions, briefing, review),
  `version` (int), `text`, `active`, `author`. Unique (`name`, `version`); one active per name.

Changes to `ChapterEntity`: add `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`, `required`,
`block_key` (nullable, origin library block), `settings` (JSON snapshot: guiding question,
rules, prompt text, required_info, checks), `removed_at` (soft delete, so revisions, findings
and restore keep working). New chapters added in an offer get key `custom_<8 hex>`.

Migration (one hand-written revision):
1. Create the tables above.
2. Add the new `offer_chapters` columns (nullable first).
3. Seed: one `ChapterBlockEntity` per entry of `quo_v1/chapters.yaml` (rules from
   `rules.yaml`), template `quo_v1` with its draft outline and published version `1`
   (`payload` from the YAML, layout bytes stored as a blob, `frame_before`/`frame_after`
   read from the layout headings), and the five prompts from `ai/prompts/*.md` as version 1.
   Version string mapping: existing workspaces keep `template_version = "quo_v1.0"`; map
   that to version 1.
4. Backfill existing `offer_chapters` rows: `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`,
   `required`, `block_key`, `settings` from the seeded quo_v1 payload. Then set NOT NULL.
Seed data lives in the migration as literals (no import of app code). After the migration,
delete `templates/quo_v1/*.yaml` and `ai/prompts/*.md`. Keep `layout.docx` only as a test
fixture under `tests/fixtures/` if tests need it.

## Phase 2: DB-backed template and prompt access
- Replace `load_template` with a `TemplateService` (`services/templates.py`) that loads a
  published `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` by (`key`, `version`) into the existing
  `TemplatePackage` shape. `layout_bytes` comes from the blob instead of a file path. Keep a
  small in-process cache keyed by (`key`, `version`); versions are immutable so no
  invalidation is needed.
- Per-offer code must use the offer's own chapters, not the template: `mark_dependent_review`,
  `services/findings.py` (rules per chapter now come from `ChapterEntity.settings`),
  `jobs/draft_chapters.py` (guiding question, rules and prompt text from `settings`),
  `services/export_snapshot.py` (order by `position`, skip `removed_at`, title/level from the
  chapter). Only `services/workspace.py` (new offer) and `jobs/export_docx.py` (layout and
  frame) still need the template version.
- `services/workspace.py`: on open, pick the latest published version of the default (or
  chosen) template and copy its outline into `offer_chapters` with `default_content` as
  revision 1.
- `ai/agents.py`: `load_prompt(name)` reads the active `PromptEntity`; the agent's
  `*_prompt_version` attributes become `"<name>@<version>"` so `GenerationRunEntity` keeps
  recording which prompt text ran. The chapter request (`ai/port.py`, `ai/render.py`) gets the
  chapter's `prompt_text` as an extra tagged section after Leitfrage and Regeln. `ai/demo.py`
  keeps working without DB prompts.

## Phase 3: Outline operations in the chapters service
Add to `services/chapters.py` (or a new `services/outline.py` if the file would pass 1000
lines; keep the DB calls where tests patch them):
- `add_chapter(offer_id, after_key, block_key | chapter_type, title)`: inserts at the given
  position, revision 1 from block default content or the empty default of the type.
- `remove_chapter(offer_id, key)`: refuses required chapters ("Pflichtkapitel können nicht
  entfernt werden."), sets `removed_at`. A removed chapter can be restored from a small
  "Entfernte Kapitel" list.
- `move_chapter(offer_id, key, new_index)`: renumbers positions in one transaction; the frame
  is not part of the list, so it can never be moved.
- `rename_chapter(offer_id, key, title)` and `set_level(offer_id, key, level)`.
- Numbering (1, 2, 2.1, …) is computed from `position` and `level` in one pure function and
  used by the UI and the export.
All handlers: `requires_offer_editor`, blocked while the chapter is protected or the offer is
archived, same conflict rules as content saves.

## Phase 4: Document view (Kapitel tab)
Rewrite `components/chapters_tab.py` into small modules under `components/chapters/`
(`outline.py`, `document.py`, `blocks/prose.py`, `blocks/table.py`, `blocks/stories.py`,
`blocks/calc.py`, `panel.py`) and split `states/chapter_state.py` into the existing state
plus mixins (`OutlineMixin`, `ChapterPanelMixin`).
- **Layout** like the screenshot: outline column (about 280px, sticky), document column
  (white page card, max width about 900px, centered, page-like padding), panel column (about
  360px, sticky, existing `inspector`). CSS in `assets/css/aq-workshop.css`.
- **Outline:** header "Gliederung" with "+ Kapitel" link button. Frame entries from the
  template in muted grey, not draggable. Chapters with number, title and a type badge
  (Text, Stories, Tabelle, Werte); selected row highlighted with `theme.ACCENT_SOFT`. Status
  badges (Blocker, Befunde, Bitte prüfen, Vorschlag, Geschützt) as small dots or badges.
  Drag handle (grip icon) on hover for movable chapters. Click scrolls the document to the
  chapter and selects it.
- **Drag and drop:** wrap `@hello-pangea/dnd` (the library Mantine's docs use for sortable
  lists) as a small Reflex component in `alloq_commons/components/sortable.py` with an
  `on_reorder(key, new_index)` event. Pin the npm version. Keyboard reordering must work
  (the library supports it). Fall back to "Nach oben" / "Nach unten" buttons in the panel.
- **Document:** every chapter is a bordered block with "<number> <title>" and the type
  badge, like the prototype. Unselected blocks render read-only from the stored content
  (prose as HTML, tables as tables, stories resolved from the map grouped by activity or
  slice, calc as bound values). Fixed frame entries render as greyed placeholder blocks with
  their heading and the note "Aus der Word-Vorlage".
- **Editing:** clicking a block selects it, gives it the accent border and mounts the editor
  for that block only (one live editor at a time). Prose uses `mn.rich_text_editor` with
  `show_toolbar` true only for the selected block and `sticky` toolbar inside the block. The
  autosave contract stays as today (debounced `autosave(key, html)`, conflict handling).
- **Toolbar per module:** shown only on the selected block.
  - Text: bold, italic, H3, H4, lists, undo, redo, plus "KI: Kürzen", "Technischer",
    "Eigene Anweisung …".
  - Tabelle: add row, remove row, add or rename column, KI suggestion.
  - User Stories: group by Aktivität / Umsetzungsschnitt (segmented control), "Story Map öffnen".
  - Werte: add or remove bound value row (only from `BOUND_FIELDS`), link to the commercials.
- **Panel (right):** "Kapiteltyp · <type>", title as heading, editable "Überschrift",
  chapter description (the block's guiding question as help text), type specific settings
  (as in the prototype for stories), Leitfrage and Regeln, AI proposal diff with
  accept/reject, findings, history, protect switch, "Nach oben" / "Nach unten",
  "Entfernen" (red, hidden for required chapters, confirmation dialog).
- **"+ Kapitel" dialog:** two tabs, "Aus Bibliothek" (active blocks not yet in the offer,
  with type badge and description) and "Leeres Kapitel" (title + type). Inserts after the
  selected chapter.

## Phase 5: Admin menu "Angebote"
New page factory `create_offer_admin_page` in `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/admin/`
(`pages.py`, `states/`, `components/`), route `/admin/offers`, registered in `app/` like the
other admin pages, sidebar entry "Angebote" (icon `file-text`) in the `ADMIN` list. Tabs:
1. **Vorlagen:** list of templates; editor with the draft outline (same sortable component,
   add blocks from the library, set required, override title and level), Word layout upload
   (`.docx`, size limit from `WorkshopConfig.max_blob_bytes`, run `check_layout()` and show
   the German error, extract frame headings before and after the anchor), "Veröffentlichen"
   creates the next immutable version, version list with author and date.
2. **Kapitelbausteine:** list and editor of chapter blocks: key (only on create), title,
   type, level, default content (edited with the same block editors as in the offer),
   Leitfrage, Regeln (list), Prompt-Ergänzung, Pflichtangaben (`required_info`), Prüfungen
   (multi select of known checks). Shows which templates use the block. Deactivate instead of
   delete when in use.
3. **Prompts:** one entry per prompt name with the active text, edit creates a new version,
   version list with diff (reuse `content/text.diff_lines`) and "Aktivieren" to roll back.
   Warn that the text must keep the data-tag rules (`<map>`, `<briefing>`, …).
Every handler `requires_admin`; every write logs at `info` without content values.

## Phase 6: Docs
Update `spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (sections 5.5 and 6.1) and the matching page under
`docs/features/` for the new outline rules, the admin menu and template versions. Run the
`docs-sync` agent at the end.

---

## Tests (write first, per phase)
- Migration: `migration-reviewer` agent; a test that the seed payload parses into
  `TemplatePackage` and every `default_content` passes `parse_content`.
- `services/templates.py`: load by version, cache, unknown version error, layout check.
- Outline service: add from block and blank, remove required refused, soft delete and
  restore, move keeps frame and positions dense, numbering function (1, 2, 2.1, 3), conflict
  and protection rules, `requires_offer_editor` in `test_workshop_authorization.py`.
- Export snapshot and docx: order by position, removed chapters skipped, added chapter
  exported with its title and level.
- Draft job and findings use per-chapter `settings` and the chapter's prompt text; prompt
  version recorded as `name@version`.
- States: outline mixin handlers (select, reorder, add dialog, remove confirm), admin states
  (create block, publish template, upload invalid layout, prompt version activate), each
  refusing non-admins.
- Update existing tests that depend on YAML files (`test_workshop_template.py`,
  `test_workshop_chapters.py`, `test_workshop_chapter_state.py`, others found by grep for
  `load_template` and `chapters.yaml`).
- Coverage ≥ 80% for the new services and states.

## Success criteria
- `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` pass; no file over 1000 lines.
- Local visual check (chrome-devtools isolated context, local test login): the Kapitel tab
  matches the prototype layout; only the selected chapter shows a toolbar; dragging a chapter
  in the outline reorders document and numbering and survives a reload; required chapters
  have no "Entfernen"; frame entries cannot be dragged; "+ Kapitel" adds a library block with
  its default content and a blank chapter.
- In `/admin/offers` an admin creates a block, adds it to a template, uploads a layout,
  publishes version 2; a new offer uses version 2, an existing offer still shows version 1.
- Editing the chapter prompt in admin changes the next AI chapter draft; the generation run
  shows the new prompt version.
- Word export of an offer with a moved and an added chapter has the right order, numbering
  and frame.
- The user runs the Alembic upgrade; Claude only hands over the command.

## Out of scope
- Story scope selection (the prototype's "Enthält Stories mit Scope" checkboxes). Scope was
  removed on purpose in the last commit; the stories panel only offers grouping.
- Moving the Branchen page into the new menu.
- Live multi-user editing in one chapter; the one-editor-per-chapter rule and conflict
  check stay.
- Migrating existing offers to a newer template version.
- New chapter types beyond prose, table, stories and calc.

# Refined prompt: Offer chapters as a document editor, templates and prompts in one "Angebote" admin menu

## Context
The "Kapitel" tab of the offer workshop is a three-column list/editor/inspector today. Each
chapter is edited on its own, the outline is fixed by `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, and
chapter prompts are hard-wired. The prototype (screenshot "KI-gestützte Bearbeitung von
Kundenanfragen") shows the target: one continuous document that feels like a word processor,
an outline that the team can extend and reorder, and a context panel per chapter type.
Admins must be able to build templates from reusable chapter blocks and maintain the AI
prompts without a code change.

The work is large. Implement it in the phases below, one phase per commit, each phase green
on `task lint`, `task typecheck` and `task test` before the next starts.

---

## Task
1. Rebuild the Kapitel tab as a document view like the prototype: outline left, all
   chapters as stacked blocks in the middle, a chapter panel right. Only the selected
   chapter is editable and shows its own toolbar.
2. Let users add chapters (from the library or blank), remove optional ones, and reorder
   them by drag and drop. Required chapters cannot be removed. The fixed legal frame of the
   Word layout stays pinned at start and end.
3. Move templates, reusable chapter blocks, rule checks, the Word layout and all AI prompts
   from code files into the database, edited in one new admin menu "Angebote".

## Load first
`alloq-implementation` (mandatory), then `reflex-state-and-architecture`,
`appkit-mantine-reference`, `appkit-commons`, `reflex-testing-state`, `german-ui-copy`.

| Area | Files | Notes |

| Template call sites | `services/chapters.py`, `services/findings.py`, `services/workspace.py`, `services/export_snapshot.py`, `jobs/draft_chapters.py`, `jobs/export_docx.py` | All call `load_template(workspace.template_key)` |

chapter is edited on its own, the outline is fixed by `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, and
chapter prompts are hard-wired. The prototype (screenshot "KI-gestützte Bearbeitung von
Kundenanfragen") shows the target: one continuous document that feels like a word processor,
an outline that the team can extend and reorder, and a context panel per chapter type.
Admins must be able to build templates from reusable chapter blocks and maintain the AI
prompts without a code change.

The work is large. Implement it in the phases below, one phase per commit, each phase green
on `task lint`, `task typecheck` and `task test` before the next starts.

---

## Task
1. Rebuild the Kapitel tab as a document view like the prototype: outline left, all
   chapters as stacked blocks in the middle, a chapter panel right. Only the selected
   chapter is editable and shows its own toolbar.
2. Let users add chapters (from the library or blank), remove optional ones, and reorder
   them by drag and drop. Required chapters cannot be removed. The fixed legal frame of the
   Word layout stays pinned at start and end.
3. Move templates, reusable chapter blocks, rule checks, the Word layout and all AI prompts
   from code files into the database, edited in one new admin menu "Angebote".

## Load first
`alloq-implementation` (mandatory), then `reflex-state-and-architecture`,
`appkit-mantine-reference`, `appkit-commons`, `reflex-testing-state`, `german-ui-copy`.

## Existing code to build on (all under `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/`)

| --- | --- | --- |
| Template loader | `export/template_package.py` | `load_template(key)` (cached) builds `TemplatePackage` from YAML + `layout.docx`; `ChapterDef`, `CHAPTER_ANCHOR`, `check_layout()` |

Repo rules that apply (from memory and CLAUDE.md):
- Offers are edited by `offer_editor` only (`requires_offer_editor`), admins do not edit offers.
  The admin menu needs the admin switch (`requires_admin` on the page and on every handler).
- Big state logic goes into mixins, not substates. Keep DB handlers in the module tests patch.
- Static layout CSS goes in `assets/css/aq-*.css`. Page popovers use `theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX`.
- Hand-written Alembic revisions in `alembic/versions/` (date-prefixed names). Never run
  `alembic upgrade`; hand the command to the user. Run the `migration-reviewer` agent.

---

## Decisions (agreed with the user)
- **Frame:** the legal blocks from the Word layout stay pinned at start and end and cannot
  be moved or removed. Required content chapters can be moved but not removed. Optional and
  added chapters can be moved and removed.
- **"+ Kapitel"** offers library blocks (with default content, rules and prompt) and a blank
  chapter of a chosen type (Text, Tabelle, User Stories, Werte).
- **Prompts:** global system prompts (chapter, map, map additions, briefing, review) are
  editable and versioned in admin. Each library block adds its own instructions on top
  (Leitfrage, Regeln, extra prompt text).
- **Admin scope now:** templates, chapter blocks, prompts, Word layout upload, rule checks.
  Branchen stays on its own page.
- **Template changes never alter existing offers** (spec 6.1). A template is edited as a
  draft and published as an immutable version. A workspace binds `template_key` +
  `template_version`. On creation the offer copies the outline and chapter settings into its
  own chapters.

---

## Phase 1: Data model and migration
New entities in a new module `workshop/template_entities.py` (keeps `entities.py` under the
line limit):
- `ChapterBlockEntity` (`offer_chapter_blocks`): `key` (unique slug), `title`,
  `chapter_type`, `level` (1 or 2), `default_content` (JSON, validated by `parse_content`),
  `guiding_question`, `content_rules` (JSON list), `prompt_text`, `required_info` (JSON list),
  `checks` (JSON list, values limited to the check names known in `services/checks.py`),
  `active`.
- `OfferTemplateEntity` (`offer_templates`): `key` (unique), `name`, `description`, `active`,
  `draft_layout_blob_id`, `frame_before` / `frame_after` (JSON lists of headings).
- `OfferTemplateChapterEntity` (`offer_template_chapters`): `template_id`, `block_id`,
  `position`, `required`, optional `title` and `level` overrides. Draft outline only.
- `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` (`offer_template_versions`): `template_id`, `number`,
  `payload` (JSON: full outline with resolved block settings, frame lists), `layout_blob_id`,
  `published_by`, `created`. Immutable.
- `PromptEntity` (`offer_prompts`): `name` (chapter, map, map_additions, briefing, review),
  `version` (int), `text`, `active`, `author`. Unique (`name`, `version`); one active per name.

Changes to `ChapterEntity`: add `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`, `required`,
`block_key` (nullable, origin library block), `settings` (JSON snapshot: guiding question,
rules, prompt text, required_info, checks), `removed_at` (soft delete, so revisions, findings
and restore keep working). New chapters added in an offer get key `custom_<8 hex>`.

Migration (one hand-written revision):
1. Create the tables above.
2. Add the new `offer_chapters` columns (nullable first).
3. Seed: one `ChapterBlockEntity` per entry of `quo_v1/chapters.yaml` (rules from
   `rules.yaml`), template `quo_v1` with its draft outline and published version `1`
   (`payload` from the YAML, layout bytes stored as a blob, `frame_before`/`frame_after`
   read from the layout headings), and the five prompts from `ai/prompts/*.md` as version 1.
   Version string mapping: existing workspaces keep `template_version = "quo_v1.0"`; map
   that to version 1.
4. Backfill existing `offer_chapters` rows: `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`,
   `required`, `block_key`, `settings` from the seeded quo_v1 payload. Then set NOT NULL.
Seed data lives in the migration as literals (no import of app code). After the migration,
delete `templates/quo_v1/*.yaml` and `ai/prompts/*.md`. Keep `layout.docx` only as a test
fixture under `tests/fixtures/` if tests need it.

## Phase 2: DB-backed template and prompt access
- Replace `load_template` with a `TemplateService` (`services/templates.py`) that loads a
  published `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` by (`key`, `version`) into the existing
  `TemplatePackage` shape. `layout_bytes` comes from the blob instead of a file path. Keep a
  small in-process cache keyed by (`key`, `version`); versions are immutable so no
  invalidation is needed.
- Per-offer code must use the offer's own chapters, not the template: `mark_dependent_review`,
  `services/findings.py` (rules per chapter now come from `ChapterEntity.settings`),
  `jobs/draft_chapters.py` (guiding question, rules and prompt text from `settings`),
  `services/export_snapshot.py` (order by `position`, skip `removed_at`, title/level from the
  chapter). Only `services/workspace.py` (new offer) and `jobs/export_docx.py` (layout and
  frame) still need the template version.
- `services/workspace.py`: on open, pick the latest published version of the default (or
  chosen) template and copy its outline into `offer_chapters` with `default_content` as
  revision 1.
- `ai/agents.py`: `load_prompt(name)` reads the active `PromptEntity`; the agent's
  `*_prompt_version` attributes become `"<name>@<version>"` so `GenerationRunEntity` keeps
  recording which prompt text ran. The chapter request (`ai/port.py`, `ai/render.py`) gets the
  chapter's `prompt_text` as an extra tagged section after Leitfrage and Regeln. `ai/demo.py`
  keeps working without DB prompts.

## Phase 3: Outline operations in the chapters service
Add to `services/chapters.py` (or a new `services/outline.py` if the file would pass 1000
lines; keep the DB calls where tests patch them):
- `add_chapter(offer_id, after_key, block_key | chapter_type, title)`: inserts at the given
  position, revision 1 from block default content or the empty default of the type.
- `remove_chapter(offer_id, key)`: refuses required chapters ("Pflichtkapitel können nicht
  entfernt werden."), sets `removed_at`. A removed chapter can be restored from a small
  "Entfernte Kapitel" list.
- `move_chapter(offer_id, key, new_index)`: renumbers positions in one transaction; the frame
  is not part of the list, so it can never be moved.
- `rename_chapter(offer_id, key, title)` and `set_level(offer_id, key, level)`.
- Numbering (1, 2, 2.1, …) is computed from `position` and `level` in one pure function and
  used by the UI and the export.
All handlers: `requires_offer_editor`, blocked while the chapter is protected or the offer is
archived, same conflict rules as content saves.

## Phase 4: Document view (Kapitel tab)
Rewrite `components/chapters_tab.py` into small modules under `components/chapters/`
(`outline.py`, `document.py`, `blocks/prose.py`, `blocks/table.py`, `blocks/stories.py`,
`blocks/calc.py`, `panel.py`) and split `states/chapter_state.py` into the existing state
plus mixins (`OutlineMixin`, `ChapterPanelMixin`).
- **Layout** like the screenshot: outline column (about 280px, sticky), document column
  (white page card, max width about 900px, centered, page-like padding), panel column (about
  360px, sticky, existing `inspector`). CSS in `assets/css/aq-workshop.css`.
- **Outline:** header "Gliederung" with "+ Kapitel" link button. Frame entries from the
  template in muted grey, not draggable. Chapters with number, title and a type badge
  (Text, Stories, Tabelle, Werte); selected row highlighted with `theme.ACCENT_SOFT`. Status
  badges (Blocker, Befunde, Bitte prüfen, Vorschlag, Geschützt) as small dots or badges.
  Drag handle (grip icon) on hover for movable chapters. Click scrolls the document to the
  chapter and selects it.
- **Drag and drop:** wrap `@hello-pangea/dnd` (the library Mantine's docs use for sortable
  lists) as a small Reflex component in `alloq_commons/components/sortable.py` with an
  `on_reorder(key, new_index)` event. Pin the npm version. Keyboard reordering must work
  (the library supports it). Fall back to "Nach oben" / "Nach unten" buttons in the panel.
- **Document:** every chapter is a bordered block with "<number> <title>" and the type
  badge, like the prototype. Unselected blocks render read-only from the stored content
  (prose as HTML, tables as tables, stories resolved from the map grouped by activity or
  slice, calc as bound values). Fixed frame entries render as greyed placeholder blocks with
  their heading and the note "Aus der Word-Vorlage".
- **Editing:** clicking a block selects it, gives it the accent border and mounts the editor
  for that block only (one live editor at a time). Prose uses `mn.rich_text_editor` with
  `show_toolbar` true only for the selected block and `sticky` toolbar inside the block. The
  autosave contract stays as today (debounced `autosave(key, html)`, conflict handling).
- **Toolbar per module:** shown only on the selected block.
  - Text: bold, italic, H3, H4, lists, undo, redo, plus "KI: Kürzen", "Technischer",
    "Eigene Anweisung …".
  - Tabelle: add row, remove row, add or rename column, KI suggestion.
  - User Stories: group by Aktivität / Umsetzungsschnitt (segmented control), "Story Map öffnen".
  - Werte: add or remove bound value row (only from `BOUND_FIELDS`), link to the commercials.
- **Panel (right):** "Kapiteltyp · <type>", title as heading, editable "Überschrift",
  chapter description (the block's guiding question as help text), type specific settings
  (as in the prototype for stories), Leitfrage and Regeln, AI proposal diff with
  accept/reject, findings, history, protect switch, "Nach oben" / "Nach unten",
  "Entfernen" (red, hidden for required chapters, confirmation dialog).
- **"+ Kapitel" dialog:** two tabs, "Aus Bibliothek" (active blocks not yet in the offer,
  with type badge and description) and "Leeres Kapitel" (title + type). Inserts after the
  selected chapter.

## Phase 5: Admin menu "Angebote"
New page factory `create_offer_admin_page` in `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/admin/`
(`pages.py`, `states/`, `components/`), route `/admin/offers`, registered in `app/` like the
other admin pages, sidebar entry "Angebote" (icon `file-text`) in the `ADMIN` list. Tabs:
1. **Vorlagen:** list of templates; editor with the draft outline (same sortable component,
   add blocks from the library, set required, override title and level), Word layout upload
   (`.docx`, size limit from `WorkshopConfig.max_blob_bytes`, run `check_layout()` and show
   the German error, extract frame headings before and after the anchor), "Veröffentlichen"
   creates the next immutable version, version list with author and date.
2. **Kapitelbausteine:** list and editor of chapter blocks: key (only on create), title,
   type, level, default content (edited with the same block editors as in the offer),
   Leitfrage, Regeln (list), Prompt-Ergänzung, Pflichtangaben (`required_info`), Prüfungen
   (multi select of known checks). Shows which templates use the block. Deactivate instead of
   delete when in use.
3. **Prompts:** one entry per prompt name with the active text, edit creates a new version,
   version list with diff (reuse `content/text.diff_lines`) and "Aktivieren" to roll back.
   Warn that the text must keep the data-tag rules (`<map>`, `<briefing>`, …).
Every handler `requires_admin`; every write logs at `info` without content values.

## Phase 6: Docs
Update `spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (sections 5.5 and 6.1) and the matching page under
`docs/features/` for the new outline rules, the admin menu and template versions. Run the
`docs-sync` agent at the end.

---

## Tests (write first, per phase)
- Migration: `migration-reviewer` agent; a test that the seed payload parses into
  `TemplatePackage` and every `default_content` passes `parse_content`.
- `services/templates.py`: load by version, cache, unknown version error, layout check.
- Outline service: add from block and blank, remove required refused, soft delete and
  restore, move keeps frame and positions dense, numbering function (1, 2, 2.1, 3), conflict
  and protection rules, `requires_offer_editor` in `test_workshop_authorization.py`.
- Export snapshot and docx: order by position, removed chapters skipped, added chapter
  exported with its title and level.
- Draft job and findings use per-chapter `settings` and the chapter's prompt text; prompt
  version recorded as `name@version`.
- States: outline mixin handlers (select, reorder, add dialog, remove confirm), admin states
  (create block, publish template, upload invalid layout, prompt version activate), each
  refusing non-admins.
- Update existing tests that depend on YAML files (`test_workshop_template.py`,
  `test_workshop_chapters.py`, `test_workshop_chapter_state.py`, others found by grep for
  `load_template` and `chapters.yaml`).
- Coverage ≥ 80% for the new services and states.

## Success criteria
- `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` pass; no file over 1000 lines.
- Local visual check (chrome-devtools isolated context, local test login): the Kapitel tab
  matches the prototype layout; only the selected chapter shows a toolbar; dragging a chapter
  in the outline reorders document and numbering and survives a reload; required chapters
  have no "Entfernen"; frame entries cannot be dragged; "+ Kapitel" adds a library block with
  its default content and a blank chapter.
- In `/admin/offers` an admin creates a block, adds it to a template, uploads a layout,
  publishes version 2; a new offer uses version 2, an existing offer still shows version 1.
- Editing the chapter prompt in admin changes the next AI chapter draft; the generation run
  shows the new prompt version.
- Word export of an offer with a moved and an added chapter has the right order, numbering
  and frame.
- The user runs the Alembic upgrade; Claude only hands over the command.

## Out of scope
- Story scope selection (the prototype's "Enthält Stories mit Scope" checkboxes). Scope was
  removed on purpose in the last commit; the stories panel only offers grouping.
- Moving the Branchen page into the new menu.
- Live multi-user editing in one chapter; the one-editor-per-chapter rule and conflict
  check stay.
- Migrating existing offers to a newer template version.
- New chapter types beyond prose, table, stories and calc.
